text:
oncall-bot: Paging eng-oncall: high P99 token latency (>1200ms) on hosted generation routes detected for the last 12m. Affected: /v1/generate (primarily customers on long-context). Alerting rule: serving.p99_tokens > 1000ms. Incident ticket INC-1975 created.

samir: I'm on it. looking at traces now — initial suspicion: continuous-batcher holding too long for big-kv cache priming. seeing long tail joins at ~1.2s when batch sizes hit 64.

lucy: FYI traffic spike correlates with a new marketing campaign for a partner running long-context completions. they suddenly increased concurrent sessions.

taylor: can we temporarily change continuous batching params? trade a bit of throughput for latency while we triage.

dave: +1 — propose lowering max_batch_wait_ms and cap max_batch_tokens for hosted tier. also adding per-customer shaping for the offending partner.

samir: quick mitigation plan:
- reduce continuous batching max_wait_ms from 25 -> 8
- set max_tokens_in_batch per-worker to 16k (was 64k)
- apply traffic-shaper to partner customer id: partner-77 to limit concurrent requests to 30
- increment soft quota for other customers to absorb spill

opsbot: Running rollout: rtm-config apply --set continuous_batch.max_wait_ms=8 --set continuous_batch.max_tokens=16384 --env=hosted-prod

lucy: I'm going to apply the rate-limit rule at the edge to throttle partner-77 to 30 rps while ops changes propagate. rdw-gateway rate-limit add --customer partner-77 --rps 30 --burst 10

samir: pushing runtime change now (canary first to 3 pods):
```
kubectl -n serving rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher-canary
rdwctl rollout update continuous-batcher --strategy=canary --canary-replicas=3
```

opsbot: Canary updated. Monitoring latency and errors for the next 90s.

lucy: edge throttle applied. partner-77 reports degraded throughput but reduced p99 latency on our end (interim). CS informed.

cs-team-bot: Notifying CS: partner-77 experiencing slower throughput due to active mitigation. Ticket INC-1975 updated.

samir: Early telemetry: p50 unchanged, p95 improved from 450ms -> 320ms, p99 dropped from 1200ms -> 520ms after canary change. errors stable.

taylor: Good. Any signs of retries/backpressure loops from clients? need to ensure we don't cause request storms.

dave: I see a spike in client retries for partner-77. CS says they saw increased 429s. We should switch to a soft throttle: return 429 with Retry-After header rather than abrupt drops. Also add guidance to partner for exponential backoff.

lucy: opsbot, can you flip gateway to soft throttle mode for partner-77? command: rdw-gateway rate-limit update --customer partner-77 --mode=soft

opsbot: Gateway updated to soft throttle mode. 429s will include Retry-After: 10s header.

samir: Next step: revert the more aggressive max_tokens limit if throughput suffers too much. Can we do gradual rollback? I can run a ramp test: 16k -> 24k -> 32k with 2m observation windows.

taylor: Sounds good. let's keep partner-77 shaped until partner agrees to change client behavior or we implement server-side request shaping per-route.

dave: also flag: disable expensive feature 'semantic-rerank' for the hosted low-latency tier temporarily — that feature adds additional scorer passes and increases token work.

lucy: command to disable:
```
rdw-features toggle --feature semantic-rerank --env hosted-prod --state off --scope low-latency
```

opsbot: Feature flag update accepted. semantic-rerank disabled for low-latency routes.

samir: telemetry after full rollout: p99 now 380ms, p95 310ms, overall throughput down ~12% for hosts running canary config. Partner-77 errors stable at ~2% with Retry-After. Looks acceptable.

taylor: prepare handoff note for next shift:
- mitigation: reduced max_wait_ms -> 8, max_tokens_in_batch -> 16k (canary -> full), gateway soft throttle partner-77 to 30rps, disabled semantic-rerank for low-latency
- current impact: p99 improved, throughput -12%, partner-77 seeing throttled requests with Retry-After
- next actions: discuss client backoff with partner cs, consider per-route micro-batching (smaller batch for long-context), gradual restore of max_tokens after client changes

lucy: documenting commands run and links to dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/d/serving/continuous-batching?org=hosted-prod

cs-team-bot: CS has emailed partner-77 with mitigation details and recommended client backoff. awaiting reply.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: @taylor please escalate to SRE channel if errors >5% or p99 > 600ms in next 3h.

taylor: noting handoff. @dave if you see retry loops spike after my shift, please revert max_tokens to 24k and re-enable semantic-rerank only for internal customers.

dave: will do. good job team. :thumbsup:

samir: closing incident provisional (keeping INC-1975 open for follow-up tasks). will create a cleanup PR to restore defaults once partner client updates are in.

opsbot: INC-1975 status -> mitigation, owners: samir,taylor, pending follow-ups: client-backoff, feature-restore, postmortem due in 48h.
